name: Latanoprost
mechanism: Prostaglandin F2α analogue - increases uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor, reducing intraocular pressure
dosing: One drop in affected eye(s) once daily in the evening. Remove contact lenses before application, reinsert after 15 minutes
contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Caution in active intraocular inflammation (uveitis, iritis), aphakia, pseudophakia with torn posterior lens capsule
interactions: Other prostaglandin eye drops (avoid concurrent use - may reduce IOP-lowering effect). Can use with other glaucoma drops (space 5 minutes apart)
monitoring: IOP monitoring (response typically seen in 3-4 weeks). Visual acuity. Fundoscopy. Visual field assessment
pregnancy: Avoid unless essential - limited data. May cause increased uterine tone and contractions
sideEffects: Iris pigmentation changes (brown, permanent), eyelash changes (lengthening, thickening, darkening), conjunctival hyperaemia, periorbital pigmentation, dry eye, blurred vision
pharmacokinetics: Prodrug, rapidly hydrolysed to active acid form in cornea, peak IOP reduction 8-12 hours, duration 24 hours
clinicalPearls: First-line for glaucoma/ocular hypertension. Use in evening (most effective). Warn about iris/eyelash changes - often cosmetically desirable but may be asymmetrical if treating one eye. Changes to iris pigmentation are permanent
indication: Open-angle glaucoma, ocular hypertension (to reduce intraocular pressure)
